tools.name: jest_run
tools.description: Jest test runner for Administration. Returns test results, preceded by a summary line with the test and suite counts. Pass/fail is derived from Jest's own JSON report, not from the process exit code: a run whose tests all passed but whose process exited non-zero afterwards is reported as a pass with the exit code called out, and a run that matched no test is reported as an error rather than a pass.

project_root.description: Absolute path to a linked git worktree of the root this server was launched in. The call runs against that tree. Omit to use the sticky root set by set_project_root, or the launch root when none is set. Supported for the native environment only.

ci.description: Run Jest in CI mode (--ci). Defaults to false. Turning it on makes the Jest config collect coverage regardless of the "coverage" argument and swaps the reporters for jest-silent-reporter plus jest-junit, which suppresses the per-test lines and the summary. Leave it off unless you need CI-identical behavior.

tools.name: set_project_root
tools.description: Set the project root every later call on this server targets, or clear it. Pass a linked git worktree of the root the server was launched in to move the server onto that tree; omit project_root to return it to the launch root. Each of php-tooling, js-admin-tooling and js-storefront-tooling is a separate process and keeps its own setting, so call this on each server you use.

project_root.description: Absolute path to a linked git worktree of the root this server was launched in. Omit to clear the setting and return the server to its launch root; the value being discarded is not validated, so this also recovers from a worktree that has been removed. Supported for the native environment only.

tools.name: cwd
tools.description: Report where this server resolves to: the effective project root and whether it came from set_project_root or from the launch, whether that root still resolves, the working directory, the environment, and the configuration files in use. Takes no parameters. Validates nothing and never fails, so it also reports a project root that has been removed.
